BURSEVI:v5p170/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p170/r1.claim: Striking their ears is a metaphor for placing a barrier against hearing: deep sleep resembles a curtain over the ears, singled out because they usually wake a solitary sleeper.

BURSEVI:v5p170/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p170/r2.claim: The response to their prayer included sleep and the subsequent turning from side to side, a hidden grace beyond ordinary causal means.
BURSEVI:v5p170/r2.anchor: وما ترتب عليه من التقليب ذات اليمين وذات الشمال وغير ذلك ايتاء رحمة

BURSEVI:v5p170/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p170/r3.claim: The cave is the place of sleep and ‘years’ its duration; the 309 years are called numbered either to magnify divine power or make the duration seem small beside God’s timeless measure.
BURSEVI:v5p170/r3.anchor: ذوات عدد هي ثلاثمائة وتسع سنين

BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r2.claim: For retreat seekers, shutting the ears blocks human speech from engraving their hearts and withdraws the senses from imprinting them.
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r2.anchor: سد آذان ظاهر أصحاب الخلوة وآذان باطنهم لئلا يقرع مسامعهم كلام الخلق

BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r3.claim: They erase prior impressions by constantly repeating ‘There is no god but God’; negation and affirmation purify and illuminate their hearts with divine knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r3.anchor: يمحون النقوش السابقة عن القلوب بملازمة استعمال كلمة الطلاسة

BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r4.claim: God manifests His essence and attributes to their hearts, annihilating them from themselves and preserving them through Him.
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r4.anchor: يتجلى تبارك وتعالى لقلوبهم بذاته وجميع صفاته فيفنيهم الله عنهم

QASHANI:18:10-11/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:10-11/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:10-11/r3.claim: Being struck on the ears is deep sleep of heedlessness from their spiritual world and perfection during immersion in bodily management until true maturity or voluntary or natural death.
QASHANI:18:10-11/r3.anchor: أنمناهم نومة الغفلة عن عالمهم وكمالهم نومة ثقيلة

QASHANI:18:10-11/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:10-11/r4.speaker: عليه السلام
QASHANI:18:10-11/r4.claim: A prophetic saying calls people asleep and says they awaken when they die.
QASHANI:18:10-11/r4.anchor: كما قال: " الناس نيام، فإذا ماتوا انتبهوا "

QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r5.claim: The highest account of the beloved is heard from the beloved himself; a poem asks Saʿd to repeat the beloved’s story because it deepens longing.
QUSHAYRI:v2p209/r5.anchor: لا تسمع قصة الأحباب أعلى وأجل مما تسمع من الأحباب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r8.claim: Striking over their ears is a vivid metaphor for heavy sleep, conveying forceful attachment and duration; ears are named because sleep deepens when hearing is suspended.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r8.anchor: فضربنا على آذانهم استعارة بديعة للإنامة المستثقلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r9.claim: The metaphor resembles expressions for imposed humiliation, poll tax, conscription, and qualities fixed on a person, illustrated with lines by al-Farazdaq, al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur, and an unnamed poet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r9.anchor: وعبر بالضرب ليدل على قوة المباشرة واللصوق واللزوم ومنه ضربت عليهم الذلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r10.claim: A hadith says Satan urinates in a man’s ear, meaning he sleeps so heavily that he does not rise at night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث: «ذلك رجل بال الشيطان في أذنه»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r11.claim: The omitted object of ḍarabnā is a barrier that prevents hearing, as in saying one built a tent over his wife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r11.anchor: ومفعول ضربنا محذوف أي حجابا من أن يسمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r12.claim: Sinīna is a time adverb governed by ḍarabnā; ʿadadan is a verbal noun used adjectivally or with an omitted preposition, meaning counted years and suggesting many.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p143#2/r12.anchor: وانتصب سنين على الظرف والعامل فيه فضربنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows ʿadadan to suggest few years because even a long period seems short to God, but the author rejects the comparison: 23:113 describes worldly life as short only when people see the promised punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويحتمل أن يريد القلة لأن الكثير قليل عنده

SULAMI:v1p402#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p402#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p402#3/r1.claim: God took away their hearing so they heard only Him and their sight so they saw only Him, leaving neither harm nor any other a share in them.
SULAMI:v1p402#3/r1.anchor: قيل : أخذنا عنهم أسماعهم حتى لا يسمعوا إلا منا

SULAMI:v1p402#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p402#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p402#3/r2.claim: God removed their human qualities, established sacred qualities, sanctified their outward and inward selves, held them in His grasp, then returned them to bodily forms and attributes when He raised them.
SULAMI:v1p402#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أخرجنا منهم صفة البشرية . وأقمناهم بصفات القدوسية ، قدسنا ظواهرهم ، وبواطنهم وجعلناهم أسرى في القبضة

SULAMI:v1p402#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p402#3/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p402#3/r3.claim: Their ears were covered so they would not hear sounds and awaken, allowing them to rest from all creatures.
SULAMI:v1p402#3/r3.anchor: وقال أيضا : إن الفائدة في الضرب على الآذان وليس للأذنان في النوم شيء إنه ضرب على آذانهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264/r1.claim: Ḍarabnā ʿalā ādhānihim means We put them to sleep.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264/r1.anchor: {فضربنا على آذانهم} أي أنمناهم. ومثله قول أبي ذر: قد ضرب الله على أصمختهم (1) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264/r2.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264/r2.claim: Abū Dharr uses the same expression, saying God struck upon their hearing.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264/r2.anchor: ومثله قول أبي ذر: قد ضرب الله على أصمختهم (1) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264/r3.claim: Al-amad means the limit or endpoint.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r1.claim: Striking a veil over their ears means they were put into deep sleep that sounds could not interrupt; hearing is one way sleep is broken, so blocking it signals its firmness.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r1.anchor: والمراد أنمناهم إنامة ثقيلة لا تنبههم فيها الأصوات بأن يجعل الضرب على الآذان كناية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r2.claim: Blocking the eyes would not convey deep sleep because sights do not wake a sleeper; at most it could suggest the onset of sleep.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r2.anchor: إذ ليس المبصرات من طرق إزالته حتى يكون سد الأبصار كناية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r3.speaker: القطب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r3.claim: Al-Qutb objects to the metonymic explanation; al-Alusi says the objection is readily answered and offers an implicit-metaphor analysis of deep sleep as a veil struck over the ears.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r3.anchor: واعترض القطب جعله كناية عما ذكر بما لا يخفى رده وخرج الآية على الإستعارة المكنية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r4.claim: Some investigators prefer reading the expression as a representational metaphor, comparing deep sleep to a veil laid over the ears.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r4.anchor: وجوز أن تكون من باب الإستعارة التمثيلية واختاره بعض المحققين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r5.claim: Some take striking the ears as preventing their function, like a ruler striking his subjects' hands; al-Alusi objects that this does not fit resurrection or establish sleep, though a proponent could intend sleep by it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r5.anchor: وتعقب بأنه مع عدم ملاءمته لما سيأتي إن شاء الله تعالى من البعث لا يدل على إرادة النوم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r6.claim: The expression may derive from striking a lock onto a door or pitching a tent over its occupant.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r6.anchor: والضرب إما من ضربت القفل على الباب أو من ضربت الخباء على ساكنه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r7.claim: The فاء parallels the response to Zachariah's prayer in 21:90; the sleep, turning, and awakening fulfill the youths' preceding supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r7.anchor: فإن الضرب المذكور وما يترتب عليه من التقليب ذات اليمين وذات الشمال والبعث

ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r8.claim: In the cave and for years are two adverbial phrases modifying the striking, one spatial and one temporal, so their combination is unobjectionable.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r8.anchor: ظرف لضربنا وكذا قوله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r9.speaker: الراغب وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r9.claim: عدد may be a verbal noun used adjectivally to mean counted, or an adjective meaning numbered, or the verbal noun of an implied verb; number can indicate either abundance or scarcity.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r9.anchor: أي ذوات عدد على أنه مصدر وصف بالتأويل الشائع وقيل إنه صفة بمعنى معدودة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r10.claim: An abundant count better displays divine power; a small count better suits the claim that the story is not uniquely astonishing, since even a long human span is like part of a day to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p211/r10.anchor: والأول هو الأنسب بإظهار كمال القدرة والثاني هو الأليق بمقام إنكار كون القصة عجبا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r1.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r1.claim: Al-Kashf says abundance fits considering the plural addressees, while scarcity fits considering the singular addressee.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r1.anchor: وفي الكشف أن الكثرة تناسب نظرا إلى المخاطبين والقلة تناسب نظرا إلى المخاطب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r2.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r2.claim: Al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salam failed to see how عدد could indicate abundance and thought scarcity impossible here; al-Alusi calls this strange for so eminent a scholar.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r2.anchor: وظن أنه لا يكون للتكثير وأن التقليل لا يمكن ههنا وهو غريب من جلالة قدره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r3.speaker: ابن حجر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r3.claim: Ibn Hajar also discusses the issue in his Fatāwā Ḥadīthiyya, but al-Alusi says he does not find his remarks persuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212/r3.anchor: وللعلامة ابن حجر في ذلك كلام ذكره في الفتاوى الحديثية لا أظنه شيئا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r8.claim: Being made to sleep is allegorized as absorption in God and annihilation in everything besides Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r8.anchor: كناية عن جعلهم مستغرقين فيه سبحانه فانين به تعالى عما سواه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r1.claim: Striking the ears means putting them to sleep; another interpretation is that sound was kept from reaching their hearing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r1.anchor: {فضربنا على آذانهم} أي: أنمناهم وألقينا عليهم النوم. وقيل: معناه منعنا نفوذ الأصوات إلى مسامعهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r2.claim: The count of years either emphasizes their number or indicates a long period, since people do not usually count a small number.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r2.anchor: وذكر العدد على سبيل التأكيد وقيل: ذكره يدل على الكثرة فإن القليل لا يعد في العادة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:11/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:11/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:11/r1.claim: God placed a barrier over their ears, meaning He put them into sleep in which sounds could not awaken them; the object is omitted idiomatically.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:11/r1.anchor: ضربنا عليهم حجابا يمنع السماع بمعنى أنمناهم إنامة لا تنبههم

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:11/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:11/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:11/r2.claim: The cave and years are adverbial complements of the sleeping action; counted can imply many or few years depending on the reference point.

NAHHAS:v2p448/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p448/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p448/r6.claim: Ear is feminine, and its damma is omitted because it is heavy; ‘years’ is a time adverb and may also appear with declension on the nūn.
NAHHAS:v2p448/r6.anchor: الواحدة أذن مؤنثة وتحذف الضمة لثقلها فتقول : أذن ^ ( سنين ) ^ ظرف ويقال : سنينا . يجعل الاعراب في النون

NAHHAS:v2p448/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p448/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p448/r7.claim: ‘A number’ is accusative as a verbal noun; it may instead modify ‘years,’ meaning counted according to al-Farrāʾ or ‘possessing a number’ according to the Basrans.
NAHHAS:v2p448/r7.anchor: عددا ) ^ نصب لأنه مصدر ، ويجوز أن يكون نعتا لسنين يكون عند الفراء بمعنى معدودة ، وعند البصريين بمعنى ذات عدد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r11.claim: Striking their ears means sealing them against sound with a deep sleep that ordinary noise could not disturb.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r11.anchor: سددناها وأمسكناها عن السمع , وكان أصله ؛ ضربنا عليها حجابا بنوم ثقيل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r12.claim: The indefinite wording for their years reflects the indeterminate duration amid the polytheism of that age.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r12.anchor: ولما كانت مدة لبثهم نكرة بما كان لأهل ذلك الزمان من الشرك , عبر بما يدل على النكرة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r13.speaker: الزجاج
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj says a counted item described as a number implies abundance, since a small number needs no counting to be understood.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r13.anchor: قال الزجاج كل شيء مما يعد إذا ذكر فيه العدد ووصف أريد كثرته

DURR-FULL:v5p370/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r2.claim: Striking their ears means God put them to sleep.
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {فضربنا على آذانهم} يقول: أرقدناهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r1.claim: The fa may connect the sleep to the youths’ prayer, making their long sleep a divine favor that saved them from torture, confirmed their truth, and later showed people the sign.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r1.anchor: تفريع هذه الجملة بالفاء إما على جملة دعائهم ، فيؤذن بأن مضمونها استجابة دعوتهم ، فجعل الله إنامتهم كرامة لهم . بأن سلمهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r2.claim: Alternatively, the fa may connect the sleep to their taking refuge in the cave, showing God quickly granted what they sought beyond their expectation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r2.anchor: وإما على جملة { إذ أوى الفتية ( الكهف : 10 ) الخ فيؤذن بأن الله عجل لهم حصول ما قصدوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r3.claim: Ḍaraba here means to place, as in placing a barrier over someone; Ibn Ashur links the usage to the Qur’anic phrase about humiliation being imposed on them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r3.anchor: والضرب : هنا بمعنى الوضع ، كما يقال : ضرب عليه حجابا ، ومنه قوله تعالى : ضربت عليهم الذلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r4.claim: The object of ‘struck’ is omitted but understood as a veil or barrier against hearing; covering the ears is a metonym for deep sleep, which prevents hearing unlike ordinary eye closure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r4.anchor: وحذف مفعول ضربنا } لظهوره ، أي ضربنا على آذانهم غشاوة أو حائلا عن السمع ، كما يقال : بنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r5.claim: Ibn Ashur calls this metonymy a Qur’anic feature unknown before this verse and an aspect of its inimitability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r5.anchor: وهذه الكناية من خصائص القرآن لم تكن معروفة قبل هذه الآية وهي من الإعجاز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r6.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r6.claim: The adjective ‘counted’ conveys many years, like ʿAʾisha’s report that the Prophet spent many nights in retreat at Ḥirāʾ before revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p268/r6.anchor: ونظيره ما في حديث بدء الوحي من قول عائشة : فكان يخرج إلى غار حراء فيتحنث فيه الليالي ذوات العدد )

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499/r5.claim: One report says God caused the youths to sleep as soon as they entered the cave, concealing their whereabouts from the kingdom.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499/r5.anchor: فروت فرقة أن الله عز وجل «ضرب على آذانهم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r2.claim: Another account says the king's searchers found the cave and advised sealing it so hunger and thirst would kill the youths; God had already put them to sleep for their protection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r2.anchor: فأمر بالدخول عليهم فهاب الرجال ذلك، فقال له بعض وزرائه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r7.claim: Striking over the ears expresses imposing sleep with force and close adherence; Arabic uses the same image for imposed humiliation, taxation, or military levies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p499#2/r7.anchor: ويعبر عن هذا ونحوه ب «الضرب» لتبين قوة المباشرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r1.claim: The line attributed to al-Farazdaq demonstrates the expression's sense of something firmly imposed or enveloping.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r2.claim: The ear is singled out because sleep strongly affects hearing and sleepers commonly wake through the ear; a Prophetic report describes Satan urinating in the ear of one who sleeps through the night.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r2.anchor: الجارحة التي منها عظم فساد النوم، وقلما ينقطع نوم نائم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r3.claim: The adjective 'counted' describes the years to intensify their number; al-Zajjaj also allows it as a cognate accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r3.anchor: وقوله عددا نعت للسنين، والقصد به العبارة عن التكثير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p108/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p108/r10.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p108/r10.claim: The pursuers found the youths in the cave, but became terrified when trying to enter; the king had the entrance blocked so they would die there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p108/r10.anchor: فكلما أراد رجل أن يدخل الكهف ارعب فقال قائل للملك أليس قلت إن قدرت عليهم قتلتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p111/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p111/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p111/r2.claim: Wahb says a shepherd opened the cave to shelter his flock from rain, and God restored the youths' souls the next morning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p111/r2.anchor: جاء راع قد أدركه المطر إلى الكهف فقال لو فتحت هذا الكهف وأدخلته غنمي من المطر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p111/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p111/r3.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p111/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sa'ib says the landowner needed a sheep pen, removed the barrier, and opened the cave.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p111/r3.anchor: احتاج صاحب الأرض التي فيها الكهف أن يبني حظسرة لغنمه فهدم ذلك السد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r1.claim: Striking over their ears means God put them to sleep and blocked their hearing, since a sleeper who hears wakes up.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى أنمناهم ومنعناهم السمع لأن النائم إذا سمع انتبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r2.claim: عددا can be an accusative verbal noun: count them as a count.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r2.anchor: أحدهما على المصدر المعنى تعد عددا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r3.claim: Alternatively, عددا modifies the years: years possessing a number.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r3.anchor: والثاني أن يكون نعتا للسنين المعنى سنين ذات عدد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r4.claim: Mentioning a count emphasizes abundance: a small number is evident, while many require counting.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114/r4.anchor: والفائدة في ذكر العدد في الشيء المعدود توكيد كثرة الشيء

SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r1.claim: The object of فضربنا is omitted, understood as the sleep-preventing barrier.
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r1.anchor: مفعوله محذوف، أي: ضربنا الحجاب المانع

SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r2.claim: على آذانهم metaphorically means sleep's persistence; ears are named because striking them brings sleep.
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r2.anchor: مفعوله محذوف، أي: ضربنا الحجاب المانع

SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r3.speaker: الأسود
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r3.claim: Al-Aswad's verse ضربت علي الأرض uses ضربت على for imposed covering or confinement.
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r3.anchor:
كقول الأسود:
3127- ومن الحوادث لا أبالك أنني

SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r4.speaker: الفرزدق
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r4.claim: Al-Farazdaq's spider verse likewise uses ضربت عليك for covering someone.
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r4.anchor:
وقال الفرزدق:
3128- ضربت عليك العنكبوت بنسجها

SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r5.claim: سنين is an adverbial complement of ضربنا.
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r5.anchor: مفعوله محذوف، أي: ضربنا الحجاب المانع

SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r6.claim: If عددا is a verbal noun, it can modify سنين with ذوات omitted, intensify the count, or be governed by an implied تعد.
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r6.anchor: مفعوله محذوف، أي: ضربنا الحجاب المانع

SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r7.claim: If عددا is an adjective meaning “counted,” it only modifies سنين.
SAMIN-DURR:18:11/r7.anchor: مفعوله محذوف، أي: ضربنا الحجاب المانع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p139#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p139#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p139#2/r1.claim: God put the youths to sleep in the cave for many counted years.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p139#2/r1.anchor: ألقينا عليهم النوم حين دخلوا إلى الكهف

JISHUMI:v6p4347/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r3.claim: ‘We struck over their ears’ is eloquent idiom for putting them to sleep; Qutrub compares it with striking someone's hand to prevent action.
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r3.anchor: والضرب معروف، (ضربنا على آذانهم) من فصيح الكلام أي: سلطت عليهم النوم،

JISHUMI:v6p4347/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r4.speaker: قطرب
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r4.claim: He compares the idiom with striking an official's or master's hand when stopping someone from acting.
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r4.anchor: قال قطرب: هو كقول العرب: ضرب الأمير على يد فلان إذا منعه عن العبث والفساد،

JISHUMI:v6p4347/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r5.speaker: الأسود بن يعفر
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r5.claim: His line about being struck upon the earth with barriers is evidence for the idiom; the source notes that he was blind.
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r5.anchor: قال الأسود بن يعفر وكان ضريرا: ومن الحوادث لا أبا لك أنني ... ضربت علي الأرض بالأسداد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r8.claim: God placed a barrier over their hearing, putting them into deep sleep in which sounds could not awaken them; the object, a covering, is omitted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r8.anchor: ضربنا عليها حجابا من أن تسمع ، يعني : أنمناهم إنامة ثقيلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r9.claim: Sinīna ʿadadan could mean many years or few, since many are enumerable; al-Zajjāj says a small number is known without counting, while a large number requires counting.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r9.anchor: فيحتمل أن يريد الكثرة وأن يريد القلة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r17.claim: Striking their ears means preventing them from hearing; this indicates they were sleeping rather than dead.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r17.anchor: والضرب على الآذان هو المنع من الاستماع , فدل بهذا على أنهم لم يموتوا وكانوا نياما

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r18.claim: سنين عددا may mean counted or enumerated years.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r19.claim: Alternatively, it means complete years without fractions of months or days.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r19.anchor: سنين كاملة ليس فيها شهور ولا أيام

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r20.claim: God blocked their hearing, though this is not itself a cause of sleep, so that they would not hear anything that could wake them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r20.anchor: وإنما ضرب الله تعالى على آذانهم وإن لم يكن ذلك من أسباب النوم لئلا يسمعوا ما يوقظهم من نومهم

MUQATIL:18:11-12/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:11-12/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:11-12/r1.claim: God seals their hearing so they sleep in the cave for three hundred and nine years.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5/r1.claim: God placed a curtain over their ears, meaning He caused deep sleep that sounds could not interrupt; the object 'barrier' is omitted.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5/r1.anchor: أي ضربنا عليها حجابا من النوم يعني أنمناهم إنامة ثقيلة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5/r2.speaker: الزجاج
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says 'counted years' means years counted because a large number needs counting; a small number can be known without counting, whereas a counted home indicates few inhabitants.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5/r2.anchor: أي تعد عددا لكثرتها لأن القليل يعلم مقداره من غير عدد

QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r1.claim: The expression describes God putting the youths to sleep and is a notably eloquent Qur'anic phrase that challenged Arab eloquence.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r1.anchor: عبارة عن إلقاء الله تعالى النوم عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the phrase as preventing them from hearing, since a sleeping person wakes when he hears.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r2.anchor: أي منعناهم عن أن يسمعوا لأن النائم إذا سمع انتبه

QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says their ears were blocked against incoming sounds by sleep.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r3.anchor: ضربنا على آذانهم بالنوم أي سددنا آذانهم عن نفوذ

QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r4.claim: A further interpretation says God answered their prayer, diverted their people's harm, and made them sleep; the readings converge in meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r4.anchor: أي فاستجبنا دعاءهم، وصرفنا عنهم شر قومهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r5.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r5.claim: Qutrub compares the idiom to striking a subject's hand to stop wrongdoing or a slave's hand to stop his trading activity.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r5.anchor: هذا كقول العرب ضرب الأمير على يد الرعية إذا منعهم الفساد

QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r6.speaker: الأسود بن يعفر
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r6.claim: Al-Aswad's verse uses the phrase 'struck the earth over me' to witness this idiom; he was blind.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r7.claim: Ears are singled out because sound most often disrupts sleep, and sleep deepens when hearing is inactive; a hadith describes Satan urinating in the ear of a long sleeper.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r7.anchor: لأنها الجارحة التي منها عظم فساد النوم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r8.claim: Adadan modifies years as counted; counting conveys a long duration since a small number needs no enumeration. It can also be an accusative of verbal noun, per Abu Ubayda.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r8.anchor: نعت للسنين أي معدودة، والقصد به العبارة عن التكثير

QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r9.claim: Abu Ubayda parses adadan as an accusative cognate object.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r9.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: «عددا» نصب على المصدر

QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r10.claim: Some take the following statement of 300 years plus nine as specifying the duration mentioned here.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:11/r10.anchor: بين الله تعالى عدد تلك السنين من بعد

ZAJJAJ:v3p271/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p271/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p271/r1.claim: Striking on their ears means preventing sound from reaching them, since hearing wakes a sleeper; thus God put them to sleep.
ZAJJAJ:v3p271/r1.anchor: معنى (ضربنا على آذانهم) منعناهم - أن يسمعوا، لأن النائم

ZAJJAJ:v3p271/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p271/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p271/r2.claim: عددا may be a cognate accusative or adjective meaning countable years; counting emphasizes a large number or group rather than one item.
ZAJJAJ:v3p271/r2.anchor: و (عددا) منصوب على ضربين: أحدهما على المصدر، المعنى نعد عددا،

RAZI-FULL:v21p70/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p70/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p70/r14.claim: “We struck upon their ears” means God put them to sleep by placing a barrier that kept awakening sounds from reaching their hearing; “barrier” is omitted from the wording.
RAZI-FULL:v21p70/r14.anchor: معناه أنمناهم وتقدير الكلام أنه تعالى ضرب على آذانهم حجابا يمنع

RAZI-FULL:v21p70/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p70/r15.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v21p70/r15.claim: Al-Zajjāj says describing countable things with “numbered” implies many, because small numbers need no enumeration.
RAZI-FULL:v21p70/r15.anchor: ذكر العدد ههنا يفيد كثرة السنين

RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r1.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj treat adadan as an adjective of years: years having a count, with either an omitted noun or the object named by its verbal noun.
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r1.anchor: نعت لسنين المعنى سنين ذات عدد أي معدودة هذا قول الفراء وقول الزجاج

RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj also allows adadan to be an accusative cognate object, meaning they were counted with counting.
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن ينتصب على المصدر ، المعنى تعد عدا

RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r2.claim: The youths remained alive and unharmed through 309 years of sleep, shielded from the sun; Rāzī treats this as a karāma.
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r2.anchor: وبقاؤهم في النوم أحياء سالمين عن الآفات مدة ثلثمائة سنة وتسع سنين

RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that a prophet must have been present in that era for the extraordinary sleep to count as a prophetic miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r4.anchor: لا بد من أن يكون فيهم أو في ذلك الزمان نبي يصير ذلك علما له

RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r5.claim: Rāzī replies that the sleep itself was ordinary, and its truth could not be verified until the exact sleepers were recognized after 309 years; therefore it cannot be a prophet’s miracle but is a gift to saints.
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r5.anchor: فامتنع جعل هذه الواقعة معجزة لأحد من الأنبياء فلم يبق إلا أن تجعل كرامة للأولياء

ASAD-NOTES:18:10#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:10#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:10#n9/r1.claim: The phrase can mean that God cut the youths off physically or metaphorically from outside sounds and bustle.
ASAD-NOTES:18:10#n9/r1.anchor: God caused them to remain cut off - physically or metaphorically - from the sounds and the bustle of the outside world

ASAD-NOTES:18:10#n9/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:10#n9/r2.speaker: classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:18:10#n9/r2.claim: Classical commentators understand the veiling of ears as putting the youths to sleep.
ASAD-NOTES:18:10#n9/r2.anchor: The classical commentators take the above phrase to mean that God "veiled their ears with sleep"

STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r11.claim: The youths' centuries-long sleep represents an intermediate realm between life and death, analogous to the state between individual death and universal resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r11.anchor: their sleep represents an intermediate realm between life and death

STUDYQURAN:18:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r1.speaker: R, Z
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r1.claim: The phrase literally says God struck them upon the ears, preventing sounds from waking them.
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r1.anchor: literally, “struck them upon the ears,” meaning that He made them incapable of hearing sounds that could awaken them (R, Z)

STUDYQURAN:18:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r2.speaker: IK, Th, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r2.claim: Another explanation is that God put them into a very deep slumber.
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r2.anchor: that He put them into a very deep slumber (IK, Th, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:18:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r3.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r3.claim: A number of years can designate either a long or a short period.
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r3.anchor: A number of years may refer to a long or short period of time (Z)

STUDYQURAN:18:11/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r4.claim: Verse 25 gives their sleep as 309 years, yet they experienced it as a day or part of one in verse 19.
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r4.anchor: v. 25 gives the number of years as 309, but the Companions of the Cave experienced this long amount of time as but a day or part of a day (v. 19)

STUDYQURAN:18:11/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r5.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r5.claim: The description indicates they remained asleep and did not die.
STUDYQURAN:18:11/r5.anchor: the companions did not die, but remained in a deep sleep (Ṭs)

TAB-FULL:v15p170/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p170/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p170/r2.claim: After their meal and conversation, God puts them to sleep in the cave for many years while their dog lies at its entrance and their provisions remain with them.
TAB-FULL:v15p170/r2.anchor: إذ ضرب الله على آذانهم في الكهف سنين عددا، وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بباب الكهف

TAB-FULL:v15p170/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p170/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p170/r4.claim: God inspires Deqianus to seal the cave to honor and preserve the youths' bodies until their revival as a sign of resurrection; two secret believers record their names and story on lead tablets in a sealed copper chest.
TAB-FULL:v15p170/r4.anchor: وأراد أن يحييهم ويجعلهم آية لأمة تستخلف من بعدهم، وأن يبين لهم أن الساعة آتية لا ريب فيها

TAB-FULL:v15p173/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p173/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p173/r3.claim: Mujahid reports that they slept in the cave for three hundred and nine years under the tyrant Deqianus.
TAB-FULL:v15p173/r3.anchor: فلبثوا في الكهف ثلاثمائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا رقدا

TAB-FULL:v15p176/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r1.claim: The phrase about striking their ears means that God put them to sleep, as the idiom of striking someone with paralysis means afflicting him with it; the years are counted and the accusative is explained by the verb.
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r1.anchor: بالفالج، بمعنى ابتلاه الله به، وأرسله عليه

TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads striking their ears as placing a barrier that made them sleep so deeply that sounds could not wake them.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r7.anchor: قال في الكشاف أي ضربنا عليها حجابا من أن تسمع يعني أنمناهم إنامة ثقيلة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r8.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r8.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains striking their ears as God imposing sleep; the author finds this more eloquent than al-Zamakhsharī's account.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r8.anchor: وقال في المجمع ومعنى ضربنا على آذانهم سلطنا عليهم النوم، وهو من الكلام البالغ في الفصاحة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r9.speaker: قطرب
TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r9.claim: Quṭrub compares the expression to an Arab idiom for an emir striking someone's hand, meaning he prevents that person from acting.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#2/r9.anchor: قال قطرب هو كقول العرب ضرب الأمير على يد فلان إذا منعه من التصرف

TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r1.claim: The author says the meaning reported by al-Majmaʿ is more eloquent than al-Zamakhshari's paraphrase.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r1.anchor: وما ذكره من المعنى أبلغ مما ذكره الزمخشري

TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r2.claim: The wording is among the Quran's eloquent expressions and cannot be translated with a meaning that matches its phrasing.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r2.anchor: وقال هذا من فصيح لغات القرآن التي لا يمكن أن يترجم بمعنى يوافق اللفظ

TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r4.claim: The phrase may also allude to a mother's gentle tapping near a child's ear to lull it, making their sleep resemble tender maternal care.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r4.anchor: وهنا معنى ثالث وإن لم يذكروه وهو أن يكون إشارة إلى ما تصنعه النساء عند إنامة الصبي

TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r5.claim: Sanin is an adverbial accusative, and ʿadad is a verbal noun meaning counted years; alternatively, a genitive complement is elided, yielding years possessing a number.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r5.anchor: والعدد مصدر كالعد بمعنى المعدود فالمعنى سنين معدودة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says counted years can suggest abundance or scarcity, since a long span is small in God's reckoning.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r6.anchor: قال في الكشاف إن توصيف السنين بالعدد يحتمل أن يراد به التكثير أو التقليل

TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r7.speaker: الزجاج
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj says a small quantity is already easy to grasp without counting, while a large quantity needs to be counted.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج إن الشيء إذا قل فهم مقدار عدده فلم يحتج أن يعد

TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r8.claim: The author prefers that counted signals a small, easily numbered span, fitting the passage's denial that the story is uniquely astonishing; the sleepers were not dead.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#3/r8.anchor: وكون الغرض من التوصيف بالعدد هو التقليل هو الملائم للسياق

TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r3.claim: The three verses summarize their flight and prayer for rescue, their counted years of sleep, and their awakening to determine which faction counted the duration.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r3.anchor: إذ رجع الشبان إلى الكهف فسألوا عند ذلك ربهم قائلين ربنا هب لنا من لدنك

TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r4.claim: Each opening verse gives one of the story's three summary elements; later verses add what happened after the people discovered them.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#5/r4.anchor: فلإجمال القصة أركان ثلاثة تتضمن كل واحدة من الآيات الثلاث واحدا منها

TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r2.claim: The youths were believers under an idolatrous tyrant who killed dissenters; they feigned hunting to flee, and a shepherd’s dog joined after the shepherd accepted their faith.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r2.anchor: وكان هؤلاء قوما مؤمنين يعبدون الله عز وجل

TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r3.claim: They entered the cave with the dog and slept until that king and city disappeared, then awoke in a new era and initially thought they had slept a day or part of one.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r3.anchor: فناموا حتى أهلك الله ذلك الملك وأهل المدينة وذهب ذلك الزمان وجاء زمان آخر وقوم آخرون

TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.claim: The cave story circulated in detailed reports from al-Qummī, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, Ibn Isḥāq, Wahb ibn Munabbih, and al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, among others.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.anchor: وردت قصة الكهف مفصلة كاملة في عدة روايات عن الصحابة والتابعين وأئمه أهل البيت

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.claim: The transmitted accounts disagree even on major features, while reports about dates, rulers, lineage, appearance, names, and the title أصحاب الرقيم diverge still more.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.anchor: من الاختلاف في متونها بحيث لا تكاد تتفق في جهة بارزه من جهات القصة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.claim: One cause is the story’s prominence among People of the Book: Quraysh learned it from them, and its Christian images and monuments spread it widely, so communities reshaped it to fit their beliefs.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.anchor: أن القصة مما اعتنت به أهل الكتاب كما يستفاد من رواياتها أن قريشا تلقتها عنهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.claim: A second cause is Muslims’ broad collection of outside reports, especially through converts such as Wahb ibn Munabbih and Kaʿb al-Aḥbār; later transmitters treated such material as prophetic reports.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.anchor: اختلط بهم قوم من علماء أهل الكتاب دخلوا في الإسلام كوهب بن منبه وكعب الأحبار

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.claim: The Qurʾān selects key lessons that serve guidance instead of supplying a complete historical account; it is a book of guidance, not history.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.anchor: فما كتاب الله بكتاب تاريخ وإنما هو كتاب هدى

TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.claim: The Qurʾān omits names, ancestry, birth, upbringing, occupations, social standing, dates, rulers, cities, persecutors, and the dog’s identity because guidance does not depend on them; historians and early exegetes filled these gaps, producing divergent accounts.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.anchor: إلى غير ذلك من الأمور التي لا يتوقف غرض الهداية على العلم بشيء منها كما يتوقف عليه غرض البحث التاريخي

TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r4.claim: The narrative presents the youths sleeping in the cave with their dog for the stated long period, protected by the cave’s position and God’s care.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r4.anchor: ثم دخلوا الكهف واستقروا على فجوة منه وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد

TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.speaker: أهل الرواية والتاريخ
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.claim: Most historians date the story between Jesus and Muḥammad; it is absent from the two Testaments, though some Muslim reports say Quraysh heard it from Jews, while Christians preserved it extensively.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.anchor: معظم أهل الرواية والتاريخ على أن القصة وقعت في الفترة بين النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وبين المسيح

TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.claim: Christian accounts resemble Ibn Isḥāq’s report from Ibn ʿAbbās in some respects but differ from Muslims on the number of sleepers, whether they had a dog, and the length of their sleep.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.anchor: أن المصادر السريانية تذكر عدد أصحاب الكهف ثمانية في حين يذكره المسلمون

TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.claim: After centuries as a ruined, forgotten site, Jordanian excavation uncovered Rujayb; the author considers its archaeological signs and some Muslim reports the strongest fit for the Qurʾānic cave.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.anchor: وقامت عدة من الأمارات والشواهد الأثرية على كونه هو كهف أصحاب الكهف المذكورين في القرآن

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.claim: Amman stands on the site of Philadelphia, a major and beautiful city before Islam that remained under Roman control from the early second century until the Muslim conquest.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.anchor: كانت هي وما والاها تحت استيلاء الروم منذ أوائل القرن الثاني الميلادي حتى فتح المسلمون الأرض المقدسة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.claim: Other proposed locations include a cave on Mount Qāsiyūn near Damascus, one at Petra, a Scandinavian cave with seven uncorrupted Roman-looking bodies, and a cave near Nakhchivan.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.anchor: والكهف الثالث كهف بجبل قاسيون بالقرب من الصالحية بدمشق الشام

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.claim: No evidence identifies any proposed cave as the Qurʾānic one; the Scandinavian and Caucasus claims conflict with the story’s Roman setting and the limits of Roman power.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.anchor: ولا شاهد يشهد على كون شيء من هذه الكهوف هو الكهف المذكور في القرآن الكريم

TABRISI:18:9-12/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:9-12/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:9-12/r4.claim: ‘We struck their ears’ means that God imposed sleep on them; the phrase is eloquent, like saying an emir struck someone’s hand to prevent action.
TABRISI:18:9-12/r4.anchor: ومعنى ضربنا على آذانهم سلطنا عليهم النوم وهو من الكلام البالغ في الفصاحة

TABRISI:18:9-12/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:9-12/r5.speaker: قطرب
TABRISI:18:9-12/r5.claim: Quṭrub compares the expression to the Arabic idiom ‘the emir struck his hand,’ meaning he prevented him from acting.
TABRISI:18:9-12/r5.anchor: قال قطرب هو كقول العرب ضرب الأمير على يد فلان إذا منعه من التصرف

TABRISI:18:9-12/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:9-12/r6.speaker: الأسود بن يعفر
TABRISI:18:9-12/r6.claim: Al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur’s line ‘the earth was struck against me with barriers’ illustrates the idiom of being blocked or confined.
TABRISI:18:9-12/r6.anchor:
قال الأسود بن يعفر وكان ضريرا:
ومن الحوادث لا أبا لك أنني
ضربت علي الأرض بالأسداد

TABRISI:18:9-12/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:9-12/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:9-12/r8.claim: ‘Years, counted’ is either an adverbial time expression with counted as a verbal noun or an adjective meaning years that are counted; Zajjāj says the extra count emphasizes that they were many.
TABRISI:18:9-12/r8.anchor: سنين نصب على الظرف وعددا منصوب على ضربين

TABRISI:18:10-12/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:10-12/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:10-12/r7.claim: God made them sleep for many counted years, answering their prayer and blocking sound from reaching them; this shows they remained alive and slept safely and peacefully.
TABRISI:18:10-12/r7.anchor: معناه أنمناهم سنين ذات عدد وتأويله فأجبنا دعاءهم وسددنا آذانهم بالنوم الغالب

TABRISI:18:10-12/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:10-12/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:10-12/r8.claim: The expression is among the Qur’an’s eloquent idioms and cannot be translated while preserving its wording’s full force.
TABRISI:18:10-12/r8.anchor: وهذا من فصيح لغات القرآن التي لا يمكن أن يترجم بمعنى يوافق اللفظ

THALABI:v6p148/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p148/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p148/r6.claim: When Daqyanus returns and threatens the believers, Tamlikha reports the danger; the youths prostrate and seek God's protection from trial.
THALABI:v6p148/r6.anchor: فزعوا ووقعوا سجودا يدعون الله عز وجل ويتضرعون ويتعوذون به من الفتنة

THALABI:v6p148/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p148/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p148/r7.claim: At sunset God causes the youths and their dog to sleep in the cave, with their provisions beside their heads.
THALABI:v6p148/r7.anchor: فبينا هم على ذلك إذ ضرب الله على آذانهم في الكهف وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بباب الكهف

THALABI:v6p148/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p148/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p148/r8.claim: Daqyanus cannot find the youths the next day, and the city's leaders accuse them of stubborn rebellion despite his offered reprieve.
THALABI:v6p148/r8.anchor: فقال له عظماء المدينة: ما أنت بحقيق أن ترحم قوما فجرة مردة عصاة

THALABI:v6p149/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p149/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p149/r2.claim: God inspires Daqyanus to seal the cave, intending to honor the youths as a sign to a later community and proof that resurrection will come.
THALABI:v6p149/r2.anchor: أراد الله عز وجل أن يكرمهم ويجعلهم آية لأمة يستخلف من بعدهم

THALABI:v6p149/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p149/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p149/r3.claim: Daqyanus orders the entrance sealed so the youths die of thirst and hunger, believing them awake; God has taken their souls in a sleep-like death.
THALABI:v6p149/r3.anchor: قد توفى الله أرواحهم وفاة النوم وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد

THALABI:v6p149/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p149/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p149/r4.claim: Two secret believers in the royal household, Biedros and Rutas, record the youths' names, lineage, and story on lead and hide it in a copper chest for future believers.
THALABI:v6p149/r4.anchor: اسم أحدهما بيدروس، واسم الآخر روتاس ائتمرا أن يكتبا شأن الفتية وأنسابهم وأسماءهم

THALABI:v6p150/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p150/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
THALABI:v6p150/r2.claim: Their people lose the youths' tracks and preserve a record of their names and disappearance in the king's treasury.
THALABI:v6p150/r2.anchor: فلما لم يقدموا كتب أحدهم في لوح: فلان وفلان أبناء ملوكنا

THALABI:v6p151/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p151/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
THALABI:v6p151/r1.claim: Wahb says the king's men are terrified whenever they try to enter the cave, so they seal the entrance and leave the youths to die.
THALABI:v6p151/r1.anchor: وكلما أراد الرجل منهم دخوله أرعب، فلم يطق أحد دخوله

THALABI:v6p151/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p151/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
THALABI:v6p151/r2.claim: A shepherd later opens the cave to shelter his flock from rain; God restores the youths' souls the next morning.
THALABI:v6p151/r2.anchor: ثم إن راعيا أدركه المطر عند الكهف فقال: لو فتحت هذا الكهف فأدخلته غنمي من المطر

THALABI:v6p151#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p151#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p151#2/r1.claim: A man named Olyas is prompted to remove the structure covering the cave so he can build a sheep pen from its stones.
THALABI:v6p151#2/r1.anchor: وكان اسم ذلك الرجل أولياس- أن يهدم ذلك البنيان الذي على فم الكهف

THALABI:v6p157/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p157/r6.claim: The phrase is a rhetorically unmatched Qur'anic expression meaning that God made the youths sleep and imposed sleep on them.
THALABI:v6p157/r6.anchor: هذا من فصيحات القرآن التي أقرت العرب بالقصور عن الإتيان بمثله

THALABI:v6p157/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p157/r7.claim: An alternative interpretation says God blocked hearing and stopped sound from reaching them, describing sleepers or the dead.
THALABI:v6p157/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه حجبناهم عن السمع، وسددنا نفوذ الصوت إلى مسامعهم

THALABI:v6p157/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p157/r8.claim: The idiom can mean that God sent an affliction upon someone, as in saying He struck him with paralysis.
THALABI:v6p157/r8.anchor: كما يقال: ضرب الله فلان بالفالج، أي ابتلاه به وأرسله عليه

THALABI:v6p157/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r9.speaker: قطرب
THALABI:v6p157/r9.claim: Qutrub compares the phrase to an Arab idiom for a ruler restraining subjects or a master stopping a servant's authorized trade.
THALABI:v6p157/r9.anchor: وقال قطرب: هو كقول العرب: ضرب الأمير علي يد الرعية

THALABI:v6p157/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r10.speaker: الأسود بن يعفر
THALABI:v6p157/r10.claim: Al-Aswad ibn Ya'far's line uses 'struck the earth upon me with barriers' as poetic evidence for the idiom.
THALABI:v6p157/r10.anchor: قال الأسود بن يعفر، وكان ضريرا: ومن الحوادث لا أبا لك أنني

THALABI:v6p157/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p157/r11.claim: Adadan means counted years and is an adjective; the author distinguishes the verbal noun from the noun for what is counted.
THALABI:v6p157/r11.anchor: سنين عددا أي معدودة، وهو نعت للسنين، فالعد المصدر، والعدد الاسم المعدود

THALABI:v6p157/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r12.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v6p157/r12.claim: Abu Ubayda parses adadan as an accusative verbal noun.
THALABI:v6p157/r12.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: هو نصب على المصدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r1.claim: They explain striking the ears as putting the youths to sleep.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r2.claim: He says God prevented them from hearing, since a sleeper wakes when he hears; Ibn Abbas describes it as striking their ears with sleep.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (أي منعناهم أن يسمعوا؛ لأن النائم إذا سمع انتبه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r3.claim: The idiom depicts overpowering sleep blocking sounds from reaching their ears; the poet's image of earth struck with barriers illustrates such prevention.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r3.anchor: والمعنى: سددنا آذانهم بالنوم الغالب عن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r4.claim: The cave phrase identifies where they slept, while counted years names the duration; numbering years implies a large quantity because small amounts need no counting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r4.anchor: وذكر العدد هاهنا يفيد كثرة السنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r5.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r5.claim: They parse adadan as an adjective meaning counted years, with either an omitted noun or a passive verbal noun used as its object.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r5.anchor: أنه نعت للسنين. المعنى: سنين ذات عدد، أي معدودة، هذا قول الفراء، والزجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538#2/r6.claim: He also allows adadan as an accusative cognate expression: We counted them with counting.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r2.claim: God sealed their hearing with sleep for a counted number of years in the cave.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r2.anchor: سددنا آذانهم بالنوم { في الكهف سنين عددا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r3.claim: God caused the youths to sleep in the cave for a counted number of years.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r3.anchor: فضربنا على آذانهم في الكهف سنين عددا

ELMALILI:18:10-12/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:10-12/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:10-12/r1.claim: The idiom of striking their ears means laying the youths down and putting them to sleep.
ELMALILI:18:10-12/r1.anchor: kulakları üzerine vurduk yani yatırdık uyuttuk

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:11/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:11/r1.claim: The phrase literally says God closed their ears; the translation ‘put them into a deep sleep’ explains that hearing was also disabled so they would not wake during that period.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:11/r1.anchor: lafzî tercümesi “kulaklarını kapattık” şeklindedir. Bu durum, uyuyan gençlerin anılan süre içinde uyanmamaları için işitme duyularının da çalışmaz hale getirildiğini ifade eder.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: These verses summarize the whole story before its details, keeping its purpose in view so secondary details do not obscure it; the Qur'an often uses this narrative pattern.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: this verse and the next two present a summary of the whole anecdote

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The idiom of patting or sealing ears developed meanings of stopping someone from hearing and affectionately lulling them to sleep, from patting a child's ears to sleep.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: to put a seal on the ears or to pat someone on the ears

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The description of sleep is an eloquent metaphor for putting them to sleep with loving care.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: an eloquent metaphor and connote putting someone to sleep in a very loving and caring manner

AKHFASH:v2p428/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p428/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p428/r2.claim: سنين عددا means years counted one by one.

FARRA:v2p134/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p134/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p134/r8.claim: فضربنا على آذانهم means that God made them sleep.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r1.claim: A literal translation of striking their ears would be unintelligible; translating it as putting them to sleep conveys the meaning rather than the wording.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r1.anchor: إن أردت أن تنقله بلفظه، لم يفهمه المنقول إليه، فإن قلت: أنمناهم سنين عددا،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba says later critics accused the Qur'an of contradiction, impossibility, faulty grammar, and disordered style, although its eloquent opponents had challenged it only as magic, soothsaying, or ancient tales.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r3.anchor: وقد اعترض كتاب الله بالطعن ملحدون ولغوا فيه وهجروا، واتبعوا ما تشابه منه ابتغاء الفتنة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r4.claim: He says he compiled explanations from tafsir, expanded them, and drew on Arab language to show metaphor and possible readings without imposing an unsupported personal interpretation.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p22/r4.anchor: فألفت هذا الكتاب، جامعا لتأويل مشكل القرآن، مستنبطا ذلك من التفسير بزيادة في الشرح

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r1.claim: The divine plural of majesty is used where the context conveys greatness and abundance; the Qur’an also uses singular forms in other contexts.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r1.anchor: وفي صيغة الجمع يؤتى بما يسمى ضمير التعظيم ويستعمل إذا كان المقام مقام تعظيم وتكثير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r3.claim: Whenever the Qur’an uses the divine plural of majesty, it is followed by a singular indicator to dispel any implication of plurality, since the Qur’an’s audience was deeply rooted in shirk.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r3.anchor: في كل موطن في القرآن الكريم وبلا استثناء إذا استعمل ضمير التعظيم لابد من أن يأتي بعده بما يدل على الإفراد

BAQILLANI:v1p268/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r1.claim: “We struck upon their ears” means that they had no sensation through their ears, without being deaf.
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r1.anchor: يريد أن لا إحساس بآذانهم من غير صمم

BAQILLANI:v1p268/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r3.claim: Talaʾum is the fitting arrangement of letters in composition, the opposite of dissonance; the “grave of Ḥarb” tongue-twister exemplifies harshly clashing sounds.
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r3.anchor: وأما التلاؤم فهو تعديل الحروف في التأليف وهو نقيض التنافر الذي هو كقول الشاعر

BAQILLANI:v1p268/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r4.claim: The author gives poetry as an example of middle-grade harmony, then says the whole Qur’an occupies the highest grade, though listeners differ in their sensitivity to it.
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r4.anchor: قالوا والمتلائم في الطبقة العليا القرآن كله وإن كان بعض الناس أحسن إحساسا له من بعض

BAQILLANI:v1p268/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r5.claim: Harmony combines pleasant sound, ease of articulation, and an effect on the heart; joined to the highest clarity and sound proof, it reveals the Qur’an’s inimitability to a discerning listener.
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r5.anchor: والتلاؤم حسن الكلام في السمع وسهولته في اللفظ ووقع المعنى في القلب وذلك كالخط الحسن

BAQILLANI:v1p268/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r6.speaker: الخليل
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r6.claim: Al-Khalīl explains dissonance as arising from sounds that are too far apart or too close in their articulation, like a leap or walking while bound.
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r6.anchor: والمتنافر ذهب الخليل إلى أنه من بعد شديد أو قرب شديد فإذا بعد فهو كالطفر

BAQILLANI:v1p268/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r7.claim: Qur’anic fawāṣil are similar or nearby ending letters that convey meaning; unlike sajʿ, their endings follow the meaning rather than forcing it.
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r7.anchor: وأما الفواصل فهي حروف متشاكلة في المقاطع يقع بها إفهام المعاني وفيها بلاغة والأسجاع عيب

BAQILLANI:v1p268/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r8.claim: Fawāṣil can use identical or neighboring letters and allow more latitude than poetic rhymes, whose effect depends on rhyme matching and meter and whose eloquence is lower.
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r8.anchor: ثم الفواصل قد تقع على حروف متجانسة كما قد تقع على حروف متقاربة ولا تحتمل القوافي ما تحتمل الفواصل

BAQILLANI:v1p268/r9.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r9.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r9.claim: Tajānis is introduced as a way of explaining forms of speech that share a common root.
BAQILLANI:v1p268/r9.anchor: وأما التجانس فهو بيان بأنواع الكلام الذي يجمعه أصل واحد

BURHAN:v1p464#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r1.claim: Qur'an recitation in a non-Arabic language is impermissible in or out of prayer, whether or not the reciter knows Arabic; the text must retain the form tied to its inimitability.
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r1.anchor: لا تجوز قراءته بالعجمية سواء أحسن العربية أم لا فى الصلاة وخارجها

BURHAN:v1p464#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r2.claim: A view attributed to Abu Hanifa allows Persian recitation without qualification, while Abu Yusuf allows it only for one unable to read Arabic; the source says Abu Hanifa's retraction is authentic.
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r2.anchor: وقيل عن أبى حنيفة تجوز قراءته بالفارسية مطلقا وعن أبى يوسف إن لم يحسن العربية لكن صح عن أبى حنيفة الرجوع عن ذلك

BURHAN:v1p464#2/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r3.claim: Consensus requires recitation in the form through which the Qur'an's inimitability operates; translation loses the Arabic's expressive precision, and even Arabic paraphrase cannot replace its challenged wording.
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r3.anchor: واستقر الإجماع على أنه تجب قراءته على هيئته التى يتعلق بها الإعجاز لنقص الترجمة عنه ولنقص غيره من الألسن عن البيان الذى اختص به

BURHAN:v1p464#2/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r4.speaker: القفال
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r4.claim: Al-Qaffal says a complete Persian translation cannot be made; he distinguishes it from tafsir, which may convey some of God's intended meaning while failing to convey the rest.

BURHAN:v1p464#2/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r6.claim: Ibn Faris's example culminates in the Sleepers' phrase فضربنا على آذانهم, whose compact Arabic expression cannot be reproduced in another tongue without explanatory expansion.
BURHAN:v1p464#2/r6.anchor: فضربنا على آذانهم في الكهف سنين عددا

BURHAN:v3p437/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p437/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p437/r1.claim: فضربنا على آذانهم is metaphor for their having no sensation there, without actual deafness.
BURHAN:v3p437/r1.anchor: يريد لا إحساس بها من غير صمم

BURHAN:v3p437/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p437/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p437/r7.claim: In istiʿāra by allusion, the borrowed term is not named; an attribute such as predation hints that the brave man is a lion, or that a scholar is an ocean. Al-Sakkaki places all figurative predication under this account.
BURHAN:v3p437/r7.anchor: وأما الاستعارة بالكناية فهي ألا يصرح بذكر المستعار بل تذكر بعض لوازمه تنبيها به عليه كقوله شجاع يفترس أقرانه وعالم يغترف منه الناس

BURHAN:v3p437/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p437/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p437/r8.claim: A subtler form stays silent about the borrowed image and signals it through a linked attribute: يفترس hints that الأسد has been metaphorically assigned to the brave man.
BURHAN:v3p437/r8.anchor: ومن أقسامها وهو دقيق أن يسكت عن ذكر المستعار ثم يومي إليه بذكر شيء من توابعه وروادفه تنبيها عليه فيقول شجاع يفترس أقرانه

RUMMANI:v1p93/r7.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p93/r7.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p93/r7.claim: The phrase means that God prevented their ears from sensation without making them deaf.
RUMMANI:v1p93/r7.anchor: حقيقته منعناهم الإحساس بآذانهم من غير صمم

RUMMANI:v1p93/r8.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p93/r8.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p93/r8.claim: The metaphor compares silencing the ears to striking a book shut; ears are named rather than eyes because closed eyes can still reopen, whereas blocked hearing prevents awakening.
RUMMANI:v1p93/r8.anchor: وإنما دل على عدم الإحساس بالضرب على الآذان دون الضرب على الأبصار

BURHAN:v3p110/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p110/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p110/r5.claim: Earlier wording can identify an omission: the alternative accounts of ما منعك, and بلاغ in لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من نهار بلاغ is completed as هذا بلاغ, stated in Ibrāhīm.
BURHAN:v3p110/r5.anchor: ومنها تقدم ما يدل على المحذوف وما في سياقه

ITQAN:v3p98/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p98/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p98/r2.claim: Linguistic metaphor uses a word outside its original assignment; one type names the whole for a part, such as 'fingers' for fingertips or 'bodies' for faces.
ITQAN:v3p98/r2.anchor: الثالث إطلاق إسم الكل على الجزء نحو
